evidence.cypher: MATCH (g:SLCGene) WHERE g.name IN $genes RETURN g.name AS gene, g.ProteinFunction AS protein_function, g.ProteinAliases AS aliases, g.Transport_type AS transport_type ORDER BY g.name LIMIT 8

MATCH (g:SLCGene)-[:IS_SOURCE]->(e:RelaEvent)<-[:IS_TARGET]-(d:Disease) WHERE g.name IN $genes OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Pathway)-[:IS_MEDIATOR]->(e) RETURN g.name AS gene, p.name AS pathway, e.rel_AB AS rel_AB, e.rel_BC AS rel_BC, CASE WHEN e.rel_AB = e.rel_BC THEN 'PROMOTION' ELSE 'SUPPRESSION' END AS gene_disease_effect, d.name AS disease, d.diseaseSort AS disease_sort, e.paper_dois AS paper_dois ORDER BY CASE WHEN toLower(d.name) CONTAINS toLower($cancer) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, d.name, g.name LIMIT 16

rows.title: Genome wide CRISPR screening reveals a role for sialylation in the tumorigenesis and chemoresistance of acute myeloid leukemia cells.
rows.abstract: Aberrant activation of cytokine and growth factor signal transduction pathways confers enhanced survival and proliferation properties to acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cells. However, the mechanisms underlying the deregulation of signaling pathways in leukemia cells are unclear. To identify genes capable of independently supporting cytokine-independent growth, we employed a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9-mediated loss-of-function screen in GM-CSF-dependent human AML TF-1 cells. More than 182 genes (p < 0.01) were found to suppress the cytokine-independent growth of TF-1 cells. Among the top hits, genes encoding key factors involved in sialylation biosynthesis were identified; these included CMAS, SLC35A1, NANS, and GNE. Knockout of either CMAS or SLC35A1 enabled cytokine-independent proliferation and survival of AML cells. Furthermore, NSG (NOD/SCID/IL2Rγ) mice injected with CMAS or SLC35A1-knockout TF-1 cells exhibited a shorter survival than mice injected with wild-type cells. Mechanistically, abrogation of sialylation biosynthesis in TF-1 cells induced a strong activation of ERK signaling, which sensitized cells to MEK inhibitors but conferred resistance to JAK inhibitors. Further, the surface level of α2,3-linked sialic acids was negatively correlated with the sensitivity of AML cell lines to MEK/ERK inhibitors. We also found that sialylation modulated the expression and stability of the CSF2 receptor. Together, these results demonstrate a novel role of sialylation in regulating oncogenic transformation and drug resistance development in leukemia. We propose that altered sialylation could serve as a biomarker for targeted anti-leukemic therapy.

rows.title: A Novel Missense Variant in Ultrarare SLC35A1-CDG Alters Cellular Glycosylation, Lipid, and Energy Metabolism Without Affecting CDG Serum Markers.
rows.abstract: SLC35A1-CDG is a very rare type of congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG) with only five cases known to date. Here, we review the literature and present new data from a sixth patient carrying the uncharacterized variant c.133A>G; p.Thr45Ala in the  gene. In addition to known clinical symptoms of SLC35A1-CDG, the patient presents with failure to thrive, short stature, café-au-lait spot, and preauricular ear tag. Even though examination of CDG markers transferrin (Tf), alpha-1-antitrypsin (A1AT), and apolipoprotein CIII (ApoCIII) revealed no abnormalities in serum, the patient's fibroblasts showed significant alterations of protein expression or glycosylation of ICAM1, GP130, and TGN46 as well as differences in staining signals of lectins MAL-I, RCAI, and SNA and deviations in LC-MS analysis of total cellular N-glycans. Transfection of CRISPR/Cas9 generated  HEK293 knockout cells with either wild-type  or the c.133A>G variant restored the cellular CMP-Neu5Ac to wild-type levels, making a direct effect of p.Thr45Ala on the function of the transporter unlikely. Instead, our results imply that the residual transporter activity of 65% is caused by a decreased stability of the mutated SLC35A1 protein. Since O-GlcNAcylation was affected as well, energy and lipid homeostasis were analyzed and found to be significantly altered. Notably, proliferation and glycosylation of the SLC35A1-deficient patient fibroblasts were enhanced by supplementation of the cell culture medium with 10 mM GlcNAc.

answer.question: bucket=pairwise candidates=['SLC35A1', 'SLC17A3']
answer.summary: [跨癌种类推] SLC35A1 has direct CRISPR/functional evidence in acute myeloid leukemia: it imports CMP-sialic acid into the Golgi and supports sialylation, which modulates CSF2 receptor stability, ERK/JAK signaling, cytokine-independent growth, and chemoresistance. Although AML is myeloid rather than B-lymphoid, both are hematopoietic malignancies and share dependencies on growth-factor/cytokine receptor signaling and glycosylation-dependent survival/immune-evasion mechanisms. Daudi cells are B-cell lymphoid, making a Golgi glycosylation transporter biologically more transferable to B-lymphoblastic leukaemia than SLC17A3, which is mainly a renal proximal-tubule organic anion/urate transporter with no lymphoid or leukemia-associated evidence. | The target cancer lacks direct TIMER/KM/PPR evidence for either candidate, so the decision relies on cross-cancer biological plausibility. SLC35A1 is linked to leukemia via genome-wide CRISPR screening and sialylation-dependent tumor survival signaling, whereas SLC17A3 has a renal transport function and no known role in lymphoid malignancy. Thus SLC35A1 is the more likely promoter of B-lymphoblastic leukaemia tumor survival, with moderate-low confidence due to lineage mismatch and mixed AML phenotype.

answer.summary: SLC35A1 encodes a Golgi CMP-sialic acid transporter involved in glycosylation and sialic-acid-dependent cell-surface modification, processes that are more directly linked to B-cell leukemia survival, immune evasion, and stress adaptation than SLC17A3. In a CRISPR/MAGECK tumor-survival context, SLC35A1 is therefore the more plausible promoter of B-lymphoblastic leukaemia tumor survival.
